title: Get 50 honest App Store and Google Play reviews from active Zedu users by Sun Nov 29
description: Listings: https://apps.apple.com/ng/app/zedu-app/id6759181591 and https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.emerj.zedu. Different from the G2/Capterra goal and from replying to reviews: this is asking real, active users for honest store reviews at the right moment (e.g. after a successful Buzz class or a cohort's first week). Done = when and where to ask (in-app, email, WhatsApp), the message copy for each, a weekly tracker, and the store-policy rules we follow. Never offer rewards for positive reviews, never gate on sentiment, never write reviews ourselves.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ask active users for honest store feedback through a policy-checked, sentiment-neutral request plan
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build one request programme that targets a verified usage milestone without pre-screening for satisfaction: define eligible active-user cohorts, permitted request moments, channel-specific copy for in-app/email/WhatsApp, suppression and opt-out rules, and a weekly aggregate tracker. Apple policy checked 22 Oct 2026 requires its provided API for in-app review prompts and rejects manipulated, filtered or incentivized feedback (https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/); Google likewise prohibits fraudulent or incentivized ratings/reviews (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9898684?hl=en). Treat engineering support for native prompts and permission to use communication channels as dependencies, not existing capabilities. Deliver one complete draft plan with neutral request copy, a platform-specific policy checklist, official store destinations, and a measurement template separating eligible users, requests, link opens where measured, and changes in public review totals. An observed review-count increase cannot be attributed to a recipient or channel without evidence. Acceptance: no rewards, rating target in the request, satisfaction gate, employee/agent-authored review, repeated pressure or guarantee of fifty reviews; support access remains independent of review choice. Measure progress toward fifty honest reviews with a dated baseline and disclose store reporting delays/attribution limits. No requests sent, app changes, personal data exports or reviews written by agents. Keep the programme one coherent task rather than splitting copy and tracking for points.

pendingIdeas.title: Measure the review request funnel by channel so published reviews can be traced
pendingIdeas.description:
The accepted workstream decides how to ask active users for honest store feedback. This is its scoreboard: one small weekly table showing which channel turns a request into a published, substantive review.

Record per week:
1. Starting rating and review count on both listings, with date, storefront and country (listing URLs are in the goal description).
2. Requests sent, split by channel (in-app prompt, email, community post, support follow-up) and by moment (e.g. after first completed session, after 7 days active).
3. Store-page visits where the store console reports them (App Store Connect / Play Console). Blank where not reported. No estimates.
4. Reviews published per listing in the week, read by hand, new vs edited.
5. Substantive-review count using a fixed definition agreed before week 1 and not changed mid-period (e.g. a review naming a specific feature or giving a concrete reason).
6. Conversion = reviews published / requests sent per channel, always with raw numerator and denominator so small numbers are not read as trends.

Honesty rules: no filtering by sentiment; every published review counts. No incentives and no asking only happy users; who is asked must not depend on how they feel. The table shows where reviews came from, not why ratings move.

Deliverable: the weekly table, written definitions for every column, and the first two weeks filled from the real listings. If requests are not yet being sent: the empty template plus definitions and the exact console/export source per column, so week 1 can start immediately.

Fit: measurement only, no code changes, uses consoles the team already has. Template and definitions within 1-2 days of acceptance.

Include: neutral review request copy that complies with Apple and Google guidelines (no incentivized reviews, no review gating), a timing strategy (when to ask - after first successful cohort session, not at sign-up), a weekly tracker template, and a response plan for negative reviews. Evidence: Zedu has apps on iOS, Android and desktop (verified at zedu.chat/download) but no visible review request mechanism in the marketing pages. Boundaries: plan and copy only, no app code changes, no review manipulation.
